job.title: Account Executive - General Insurance
job.description:
Own your book. Get to know the people behind it!
 
A good renewal starts with a conversation. What has changed for the client? Does their cover still fit? What do they need to understand before they make a decision?
 
Hinchen Recruitment Group is partnering with an established, privately owned insurance brokerage in Upper Mount Gravatt to appoint an Account Executive. You'll take over a portfolio of around 500 policies, with approximately 60% domestic and strata and 40% commercial. The commercial book is predominantly SME, spanning risks such as trade liability and professional indemnity.
 
Around 80% of the role is focused on renewals and servicing existing clients, with the balance spent following up referrals, responding to enquiries and identifying opportunities within the book. You'll have an introduction to the portfolio, administrative support for pre-renewals and a dedicated Claims Manager who handles most claims. Senior brokers are available to assist with complex placements.
 
What you'll do
  • Manage renewals from the first client conversation through to insurer negotiations, placement and documentation.
  • Handle quotes, endorsements and day-to-day enquiries, explaining cover and options in plain English.
  • Stay close to clients so you can identify changing risks and gaps in cover.
  • Follow up referrals and enquiries and convert suitable opportunities into new business.
  • Maintain accurate file notes and compliant records, and bring in senior brokers when a placement needs specialist input.
What you'll bring
 
You hold a Tier 1 Insurance Broking qualification and have hands-on general insurance broking experience. You're comfortable running renewals independently, negotiating with insurers and keeping clients informed when several deadlines are competing for your attention.
 
Experience across a mixed domestic, strata and SME commercial book will help you settle in quickly. Familiarity with Insight, Sunrise, SCTP or comparable broking systems is valued. A Diploma of Insurance Broking is well regarded, and study support is available if you're looking to complete it.
 
What's on offer
  • $90,000-$120,000 base + super, depending on experience.
  • Quarterly Performance bonus tied to revenue above target.
  • 9 am to 5 pm hours Mon - Fri and one work-from-home day per week after probation.
This is an exciting opportunity to join a well established, highly awarded and highly respected business in growth.

If you’d like to hear more about the book, the team or the bonus structure before applying, contact Louisa Hinchen at Hinchen Recruitment Group for a confidential conversation on 0459 991 061.

Or, if your ready to take ownership of an established insurance portfolio with experienced brokers and a dedicated Claims Manager and administrative support behind you, apply now by following the link and ideally submit your resume in word format.

job.title: Wellbeing Practitioner - Social Worker
job.description:
Looking for meaningful Social Work without the hospital pace, shift work or constant pressure of an ED environment?

This could be the change you have been looking for.

Our client is an industry-leading not-for-profit organisation that has built a strong reputation for the quality of its services, the professionalism of its teams and, just as importantly, the way it looks after its people.

This is a Monday–Friday, office-based Wellbeing Practitioner role working within an established multidisciplinary environment.

No shift work.

No ED.

No running between community appointments all day.

Instead, you will be working from a professional office environment with a team around you, access to supervision and the opportunity to do meaningful work while still having some structure around your week.

What really stands out about this organisation is the culture.

They talk a lot about values and more importantly, you can see those values in the way the teams work together, how leaders support their people and how seriously they take the quality of the service they provide.

These are not just words on a wall.

The Opportunity
As a Wellbeing Practitioner, you will work directly with clients experiencing a range of wellbeing, social and practical challenges.
The role combines psychosocial assessment, support planning, referrals, service coordination, risk assessment and ongoing client engagement.

You will work alongside experienced practitioners across a multidisciplinary environment and have access to regular supervision, reflective practice and professional development.

Your day may include:

• Completing psychosocial assessments
• Working with clients to identify goals and priorities
• Developing practical support plans
• Coordinating health, mental health, housing, financial and community supports
• Working closely with internal practitioners and external providers
• Supporting clients through complex systems and periods of change
• Identifying and escalating risk where required
• Maintaining accurate and timely documentation
• Participating in supervision, team meetings and professional development
Who We’re Looking For
You may currently be working in:
• Hospital Social Work
• Mental health
• Community services
• Case management - (18-20 Caseload)
• Psychosocial support
• Child and family services
• Rehabilitation
• Another related health or human services environment

You do not need to come from exactly the same background.
What matters is that you are a qualified practitioner who can build strong relationships, think professionally, work through complexity and genuinely care about the quality of the support you provide.

You will need:
• A relevant degree in Social Work, Human Services, Health Sciences, Psychology or equivalent enabling professional membership or registration eligibility through AASW, AHPRA or PACFA
• Minimum 2 years’ relevant experience
• Experience completing psychosocial assessments and support planning
• Strong understanding of trauma-informed and strengths-based practice
• Confidence working with complex presentations and risk
• Strong written communication and documentation skills
• Ability to work autonomously while contributing to a multidisciplinary team
• Current driver’s licence

What’s On Offer
• $91,264 + super
• Salary packaging benefits
• Performance-based incentive opportunities
• Monday–Friday office hours
• Office-based environment
• No shift work or ED environment
• Structured supervision and reflective practice
• Ongoing professional development
• Career progression within a growing organisation
• Multidisciplinary team support
• Strong leadership and workplace culture
• An established, purpose-driven NFP with a genuine commitment to its values

If you are looking for a role where you can continue developing professionally, work with a strong team and be part of an organisation that genuinely lives its values, I would love to have a conversation.

Loss of structure.
Loss of identity.
Complex physical, mental and social needs.
This is where you come in.

job.title: Business Development Executive - Own the WA Market
job.description:
Our client is part of a global leader in water purification and filtration, providing innovative hydration solutions across hospitality, commercial workplaces, healthcare, education, fitness and a broad range of business environments.

With an established customer base already in Western Australia and significant opportunity still available across the market, they are now looking for a driven Business Development Executive to take ownership of new business growth across WA.

This is a rare opportunity to take ownership of an enormous WA new-business market.

You won’t be boxed into one vertical, one industry or a small postcode territory, and you won’t have a team of BDMs competing for the same prospects.

Across hospitality and commercial markets, the opportunity is broad — restaurants, hotels, cafes, offices, healthcare, fitness, education and virtually any workplace where the solution fits.

You’ll have the freedom to identify where the opportunity is, build your own network, create your own pipeline and make the market your own.
The more you build, the more you earn.

For a genuine new-business hunter who wants autonomy and likes being directly rewarded for the business they create, opportunities like this don’t come around often.

Hospitality experience will be highly regarded.

You might already be selling into restaurants, cafes, hotels or bars, or you may have previously worked in hospitality before moving into sales.
You may equally come from venue management, foodservice, beverages, coffee, FMCG or another customer-facing commercial environment.

What matters most is that you are comfortable approaching new people, opening doors, building relationships and creating business rather than waiting for opportunities to come to you.

Why this role?
  • $75,000 + Super base salary
  • $15,000 car allowance
  • Uncapped commission
  • OTE circa $125,000+
  • Genuine earning potential well beyond OTE for strong performers
  • Rare opportunity to take ownership of a broad WA new-business market
  • Established WA customer footprint with significant untapped opportunity
  • Blend of hospitality and commercial sales
  • Highly autonomous field-based role
  • Flexibility to manage your own day
  • Comprehensive onboarding and structured sales training
  • Support from experienced interstate and local team members
  • Access to an established Belmont office and service team
  • Global organisation with established products and strong market presence
  • Career development and progression opportunities
“Once people get through the first six months, they tend not to leave. The longer you’re with us, the easier it becomes and as you build your network, you build your pipeline, and sales bring sales.” — General Manager

About the role
This is a highly autonomous, field-based new-business role with a broad WA market to develop.

This is not an account-management position. The focus is on finding opportunities, opening new doors and building your own pipeline.
You’ll be responsible for developing new business across both hospitality and commercial environments.

Your market could include restaurants, cafes, bars, hotels, commercial offices, gyms, healthcare environments, education, workplaces and a wide range of other businesses where quality drinking water solutions can add value.

You’ll use a combination of face-to-face prospecting, networking, referrals, direct outreach and your own market knowledge to build your pipeline.
WA already has a significant customer base, but with the role having been vacant for a period there is substantial opportunity for the right person to get into market and build momentum quickly.

You’ll work with business owners, venue operators and commercial decision-makers to understand their needs, recommend the appropriate solution and manage opportunities from the first conversation through to installation.
The role gives you genuine autonomy to manage your own day and market, while still providing the onboarding, structure and support you need to succeed.

Key responsibilities
In this role, you will:
  • Identify and develop new business opportunities across hospitality and commercial markets
  • Build and manage your own sales pipeline
  • Proactively hunt for new customers and open new doors
  • Engage with prospective customers through face-to-face activity, phone, networking and referrals
  • Develop relationships with restaurant, cafe, hotel and venue operators
  • Build relationships with business owners and commercial decision-makers
  • Understand customer needs and recommend appropriate solutions
  • Conduct customer meetings, product demonstrations and presentations
  • Negotiate and close new sales opportunities
  • Manage opportunities from first conversation through to installation
  • Maintain accurate customer and pipeline information
  • Work closely with internal service and support teams
  • Develop relationships that generate repeat business and referrals
  • Take ownership of your market and identify new areas for growth
About you
You may already be working as a Business Development Executive, BDM, Sales Representative, Territory Manager, Account Executive or Field Sales Representative.
But your job title is not the most important part.
For this WA opportunity, we are particularly interested in people who understand hospitality and are comfortable operating in that environment.
You may have worked in restaurants, bars, cafes, hotels or venues earlier in your career before moving into sales.
You may currently be selling food, beverages, coffee, equipment, FMCG or other products into the hospitality sector.
You might even be a strong venue manager or hospitality operator looking to move into a commercial sales career where your industry knowledge, commercial awareness and ability to connect with people can be rewarded.
Above all, you need to enjoy hunting for new business.
You’ll be comfortable walking into a venue or business, introducing yourself, starting a conversation and identifying an opportunity.
You are commercially minded, self-motivated and comfortable managing your own time, activity and priorities.
You enjoy having ownership of your results and the freedom to build your own market.
You’ll also be open to learning and comfortable working within a proven sales process that provides the structure and support to help you succeed.

What you will bring
  • Hospitality experience or strong exposure to the hospitality sector
  • A genuine new-business hunter mentality
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills
  • Confidence engaging with new customers face-to-face
  • A proactive approach to opening doors and developing new business
  • Ability to build rapport quickly with different customer types
  • Strong self-motivation and personal accountability
  • Commercial awareness and an understanding of customer needs
  • Confidence working autonomously in the field
  • Ability to manage your own time, activity and pipeline
  • Resilience and a results-focused mindset
  • Willingness to learn and work within a proven sales process
  • Previous B2B or field sales experience highly regarded
  • Hospitality operators with strong commercial capability are also encouraged to apply
The environment
This is a role for someone who enjoys being out in the market rather than sitting behind a desk.

You’ll spend your time meeting customers, opening doors, building relationships, creating opportunities and developing your network across WA.
The business has an established office in Belmont, along with experienced service and support team members.

You’ll have the flexibility to use the office when it works for you, work from home when appropriate, and spend the majority of your customer-facing time out in market.

You’ll also receive structured onboarding and initial support from experienced BDMs and sales leaders to help you understand the products, the sales process and how the business goes to market.

At $75K base + $15K car allowance + uncapped commission, OTE is circa $125K+.

Importantly, that is not an earnings ceiling.

Strong performers within the business earn substantially more, with genuinely uncapped commission rewarding those who consistently create opportunities and convert business.

If you are looking for a role where you can combine your hospitality knowledge with genuine new-business sales, take ownership of a huge market and be directly rewarded for the results you create, we would love to hear from you.
Please submit your application including a current resume.

job.description:
OOSH Coordinator (Diploma Qual)

If you’re a Diploma-qualified educator who enjoys leading a team, building great programs, and making a real impact in a community then this is a rare chance to step into a Coordinator role with genuine purpose.

This not-for-profit service is ready to re-open and grow their OOSH program and they’re looking for a confident, capable Coordinator to bring it to life.

Importantly, if you’re looking for more hours, the service can combine OOSH with additional hours in the preschool (ELC) to create a full-time role for the right person.

Why you’ll love it here
  • Full-time option available: combine OOSH + extra ELC hours (for the right candidate)
  • School-term friendly base hours: 2:00pm–6:00pm, Monday to Friday
  • Full-time hours available in school holidays (vacation care)
  • Great hourly rate: $34–$38/hour + super (aligned to experience)
  • NFP salary packaging: boost your take-home pay
  • Relocation support may be available for the right candidate
  • A genuinely supportive team culture — people back each other, communicate openly, and take pride in quality care

  • Coordinate the day-to-day delivery of the OOSH service (after school + vacation care)
  • Lead and mentor educators to deliver safe, engaging, inclusive programs
  • Design and deliver programming aligned to My Time, Our Place (MTOP)

You will bring
  • Diploma of Early Childhood Education and Care (or equivalent)

  • A calm, practical leadership style with clear communication

Note: Prior “OOSH Coordinator” title experience is not essential — this can suit a strong Diploma educator ready for their next step (ideally ~2 years post-Diploma experience).

job.title: Team Leader - Housing Support
job.description:
This is an opportunity to step into a meaningful leadership role with a highly regarded, values-driven not-for-profit organisation supporting veterans and their families across Queensland and the Northern Territory
The role leads a team delivering housing and homelessness support to people who may be experiencing financial hardship, housing instability, homelessness or complex personal circumstances. The service is holistic, practical and deeply person-centred, with a strong focus on dignity, respect and long-term outcomes.

This position will suit an experienced Team Leader, Senior Practitioner or Senior Case Manager who enjoys leading people, improving practice and creating the structure needed for high-quality service delivery.

Why this role?

• $110,000 + super + salary packaging benefits
• Brisbane based
• Leadership-focused role with a small, manageable caseload
• Lead a passionate housing support team across multiple locations (QLD & NT)
• Opportunity to influence practice standards, process improvement and service delivery
• Join a nationally respected, purpose-driven Not for Profit organisation
• Strong systems, structure and operational support
• Support meaningful outcomes for veterans and their families
• Collaborative, values-led and supportive team culture
• Opportunity to contribute to service improvement, process development and best-practice case management
• Exposure across metro, regional and multidisciplinary service environments
• Travel opportunities across regional locations as required
• Stable organisation with strong leadership and long-term community impact

As Team Leader – Housing Support, you will provide day-to-day leadership to a team of Housing Support Practitioners delivering support to veterans and families who are at risk of, or experiencing, homelessness.
The program provides case management, housing support, financial hardship support and, in some cases, funded crisis accommodation. The role has a strong operational focus, including case oversight, referral allocation, quality assurance, staff supervision, stakeholder engagement, financial approvals and compliance with service delivery requirements.
This is primarily a leadership and operational oversight role, with a small caseload held as part of a broader multidisciplinary team.
The role reports to the Wellbeing Manager, Veteran Services and is accountable for leading Housing Support Practitioners within the broader wellbeing team. The position includes leadership across multiple locations, regular case reviews, monitoring caseloads, ensuring compliance, stakeholder collaboration and oversight of case plans and expenditure.

Key responsibilities
In this role, you will:
• Lead, coach and support Housing Support Practitioners across multiple locations
• Provide supervision, case reviews and guidance on complex matters
• Review referrals and allocate work across the team
• Monitor caseloads, workload, risks and team capacity
• Support client-centred, strengths-based housing support and case management
• Review and approve case plans, financial assistance and support requests
• Ensure accurate documentation, case notes and compliance within client systems
• Build strong relationships with internal teams, community organisations, government bodies and specialist housing providers
• Support team culture, performance, engagement and professional development
• Contribute to service improvement, process development and consistent practice standards

About you
You will bring a strong combination of people leadership, case management experience and operational discipline.
You may come from housing, homelessness, community services, mental health, family support, domestic and family violence, AOD, veteran services or another complex case management environment.
You do not need to have worked in veteran services before. What matters is your ability to lead a team, work within structured service delivery requirements, manage competing priorities and support people through complex and sensitive circumstances.

You will bring:
• A degree in Human Services, Health Sciences, Social Work, Psychology, Counselling or a related discipline
• Eligibility for registration or professional membership with a relevant body such as AASW, AHPRA or PACFA
• 2–3+ years’ experience in a Team Leader, Senior Practitioner, Senior Case Manager or similar leadership role (ideally lead a remote multi-state team)
• Strong experience in person-centred and strengths-based case management
• Demonstrated ability to lead, mentor and motivate staff
• Strong attention to detail, documentation and compliance
• Sound judgement when working with complex or sensitive client situations
• Ability to work within policies, procedures, legislative requirements and budget parameters
• Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills
• A Queensland C Class driver’s licence
• Flexibility to travel when required

Experience in specialist homelessness services or community services will be highly regarded. An understanding of the ADF, Defence or veteran community would also be beneficial, but is not essential.

The environment
You will be joining a supportive and collaborative team that is genuinely committed to the people they support.
This is a role with heart, but it also requires structure. The successful candidate will be comfortable working in a process-driven environment where case notes, compliance, financial approvals, service standards and clear communication all matter.
The best fit will be someone who can bring empathy and professionalism, while also creating consistency, accountability and confidence across the team.

job.title: Wellbeing Practitioner
job.description:
Do work that truly matters — with professional depth and real impact.
  
This organisation is expanding its Veteran Services team and is seeking experienced Wellbeing Practitioners to deliver trauma-informed, strengths-based case management to veterans and their families with complex needs.
  
This is a professionally governed role involving psychosocial assessment, care coordination, ethical decision-making, and evidence-based practice. You will work within structured frameworks to support clients to navigate complex health and social systems, build wellbeing, and achieve sustainable outcomes.
  
The Opportunity
As a Wellbeing Practitioner, you will deliver short- and long-term case management interventions, including psychosocial assessment, individualised care planning, health literacy development, and access to financial and emergency supports. You will work collaboratively with internal teams and external partners to ensure coordinated, veteran-centred care.
  
Key Responsibilities
• Conduct holistic psychosocial assessments and develop individualised case management plans
• Deliver trauma-informed, strengths-based, person-centred case management
• Manage an active caseload of approximately 15–20 clients based on complexity and need
• Coordinate referrals across health, mental health, housing, financial and community services
• Support access to emergency relief, applications for assistance and other wellbeing support packages
• Promote health literacy and guide clients through complex service systems
• Identify, manage and escalate risk and high-complexity cases appropriately
• Maintain accurate, timely and confidential case notes and documentation within CRM systems
• Build strong collaborative relationships with partners including DVA, Open Arms, health providers, housing services and community organisations
• Participate in supervision, peer reviews, team meetings and professional development activities
  
The Cohort
You will support veterans who may be experiencing mental health challenges, social isolation, financial stress, transition from institutional settings, or the impacts of trauma and complex life stressors. This is meaningful, complex work requiring sound professional judgement, emotional resilience, and strong ethical boundaries.
  
What We’re Looking For
  
Essential:
• Degree in Human Services, Health Sciences, Social Work, Psychology or equivalent enabling eligibility for professional membership/registration (e.g. AASW, AHPRA, PACFA)
• Minimum 2 years’ experience in a similar case management, wellbeing or psychosocial support role
• Strong experience in strengths-based and trauma-informed practice
• Ability to conduct psychosocial assessments and develop structured care plans
• High-level written and verbal communication skills and strong attention to detail
• Ability to work autonomously within governance, ethical and practice frameworks
• Willingness to undertake relevant advocacy or practice framework training
• Current driver’s licence
  
Highly Regarded:
• Experience working with veterans, Defence, or complex trauma cohorts
• Knowledge of health, mental health, and social service systems
• Strong clinical reasoning, ethical decision-making and risk management capability
  
What’s On Offer
• Competitive salary + super + salary packaging

Are you an experienced environmental professional who enjoys getting out on site, solving practical challenges and working alongside operational leaders to make a genuine difference?

Our client is Australia's largest vertically integrated construction materials company, and today they are seeking an experienced Environment Business Partner to support their extensive Queensland operations.

This is an opportunity to combine your technical environmental expertise with a highly visible, operationally focused business partnering role, influencing environmental compliance, risk management and continuous improvement across a diverse network of quarries, concrete batching plants, asphalt operations and recycling facilities.

Reporting to the Senior Environment Business Partner, you will work closely with Quarry Managers, Regional Managers and operational teams, providing practical advice, coaching and guidance to strengthen environmental capability and accountability.
 
This is not a desk-based compliance role.  Success will come from your ability to establish credibility on site, understand operational challenges and translate environmental obligations into practical solutions that support both compliance and business performance.
 
Your key responsibilities will include:
  • Partner with operational leaders to strengthen environmental compliance, risk management and site performance.
  • Conduct site inspections, environmental audits and assurance activities, identifying risks and improvement opportunities.
  • Provide practical advice on environmental approvals, licence conditions, legislation and operational requirements.
  • Support environmental monitoring programs, including water, dust, noise, emissions and other site-specific obligations.
  • Coordinate environmental compliance reporting, including annual returns, monitoring results and National Pollutant Inventory (NPI) submissions.
  • Investigate environmental incidents and complaints, identify root causes and support corrective actions.
  • Review environmental management plans, approvals and operating conditions to maintain compliance.
  • Advise operational teams on land disturbance, vegetation clearing, water management and other site activities.
  • Coach and educate site personnel, building environmental capability, ownership and accountability.
  • Work with consultants, regulators and internal stakeholders to resolve environmental matters and support continuous improvement.
  • Contribute to environmental improvement initiatives and the implementation of Boral's broader environmental strategy.
What you will bring to this role:
  • You will be a technically capable environmental professional with the confidence, initiative and interpersonal skills to influence outcomes in a complex operational environment.
  • A relevant tertiary qualification in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Management or a related discipline.
  • Approximately five years or more of environmental experience within heavy industry, mining, quarrying, construction, manufacturing, waste management or a regulatory environment.
  • Strong working knowledge of environmental legislation, approvals, licence conditions and compliance requirements.
  • Practical experience with environmental monitoring, inspections, incident investigations, reporting and risk management.
  • The ability to interpret technical and regulatory requirements and translate them into practical operational solutions.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills, with the confidence to advise, coach and influence site and regional management teams.
  • A proactive, self-directed approach, with the ability to prioritise competing activities across multiple locations.
  • Sound commercial judgement and an appreciation of the need to balance environmental compliance with operational realities.
  • Experience working across multiple operational sites, particularly within quarrying, mining or other extractive industries, will be highly regarded.
  • Exposure to environmental regulator engagement, approvals or licence variations would also be advantageous.
  • Importantly, you will enjoy being visible in the business, building trusted relationships and taking ownership of delivering outcomes.

Location and Travel

job.title: Business Development Executive - New Business Sales
job.description:
Our client is part of a global leader in water purification and filtration, providing innovative hydration solutions across commercial workplaces, healthcare, education, fitness, hospitality and a broad range of business environments.

With significant growth underway across Australia, they are now looking for a driven Business Development Executive to help grow their presence across Brisbane.

This is a genuine new-business role for someone who enjoys building relationships, creating opportunities and taking ownership of their market.

You’ll have the autonomy to manage your own day, backed by a proven sales process, strong onboarding and an established global organisation.

You don’t necessarily need to come from the water industry or even from a traditional BDM background.

Some of the strongest performers in the business have come from hospitality, retail, sales-adjacent roles and completely different industries. What matters is your ability to connect with people, understand what they need, identify an opportunity and build a relationship that leads to business.

Why this role?
  • $75,000 + Super base salary
  • $15,000 car allowance
  • Uncapped monthly commission
  • OTE circa $125,000
  • Genuine earning potential beyond OTE for strong performers
  • Highly autonomous field-based role
  • Flexibility to manage your own day
  • Significant opportunity across the Brisbane market
  • Comprehensive onboarding and structured sales training
  • Global organisation with established products and strong market presence
  • Opportunity to join the business during a significant growth phase
  • Career development and progression opportunities
  • Supportive and experienced leadership team
 “Once people get through the first six months, they tend not to leave. The longer you’re with us, the easier it becomes and as you build your network, you build your pipeline, and sales bring sales.” — General Manager
 
About the role
This is a highly autonomous, field-based sales role with plenty of scope to make it your own.
A key focus will be developing new business, building your own network and identifying opportunities across a broad commercial market.
You’ll use a mix of prospecting, networking, referrals and face-to-face engagement to build relationships and grow your customer base.
That could include commercial offices, gyms, healthcare environments, warehouses, Early Learning Centers, workplaces and a wide range of other businesses where quality drinking water solutions can add value.

You’ll work with decision-makers to understand their needs, recommend the right solution and manage opportunities through the sales process from initial conversation through to installation.

The role gives you genuine freedom to manage your day and pursue opportunities, while still providing the structure, training and support to help you succeed.

Key responsibilities
In this role, you will:
  • Identify and develop new business opportunities
  • Build and manage your own sales pipeline
  • Engage with prospective customers through phone, networking and face-to-face activity
  • Build strong relationships with business owners and commercial decision-makers
  • Understand customer needs and recommend appropriate solutions
  • Conduct customer meetings, product demonstrations and presentations
  • Negotiate and close new sales opportunities
  • Manage opportunities through the sales process from first contact to installation
  • Maintain accurate customer and pipeline information
  • Work closely with internal teams to ensure a positive customer experience
  • Develop relationships that support repeat business and referrals
  • Take ownership of your market and identify new areas for growth
About you
You may already be working as a Sales Representative, Sales Consultant, Territory Sales Representative, Business Development Executive, Account Executive or BDM.

But your job title is not the most important part.

You may equally come from retail sales, hospitality, field sales, promotional sales or have previously run your own business.

The business has successfully hired people from a wide range of backgrounds because the common denominator is not industry experience, but it is attitude, commercial awareness and the ability to connect with people.

You’ll be someone who enjoys meeting new people, building rapport and identifying opportunities.

You are self-motivated, commercially minded and comfortable managing your own time and priorities.

You like having ownership of your results and the freedom to build your market in a way that works.

You will also be open to learning and comfortable working within a proven sales process that gives you the tools and support to succeed.

What you will bring
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills
  • Confidence engaging with new customers
  • A proactive approach to developing new business
  • Ability to build rapport quickly and understand customer needs
  • Strong self-motivation and personal accountability
  • Commercial awareness and an understanding of the sales process
  • Confidence working autonomously in the field
  • Ability to manage your own time, activity and pipeline
  • Resilience and a results-focused mindset
  • Willingness to learn and work within a proven sales process
  • Previous sales experience highly regarded, although the right capability may come from outside traditional B2B sales
The environment
This is a role for someone who enjoys being out in the market rather than sitting behind a desk all day.

You’ll spend your time meeting customers, building relationships, developing opportunities and growing your network.

Our client offers genuine autonomy, supported by a comprehensive induction, product training and a structured approach to helping new starters build confidence and momentum.

The Brisbane market offers significant growth potential, with a broad range of industries and customers still available to develop.

At $75K base + $15K car allowance + uncapped commission, the advertised OTE is around $125K.

Importantly, that is not an earnings ceiling.

For people who consistently build relationships, create opportunities and convert business, there is genuine scope to earn considerably more.

If you are looking for a role where you can own your day, build your own market and be directly rewarded for the results you create, we would love to hear from you.

Please submit your application including a current resume.
Paul@hinchen.com.au
Or for a confidential discussion, please call Paul on 0422 963 025

job.title: Environmental Business Partner
job.description:
Our client is an established Australian business in the construction materials sector. This is an opportunity to apply your environmental expertise across a diverse operational portfolio and help site teams turn compliance requirements into practical action.

Based at Port Melbourne and reporting to the Senior Environmental Business Partner, you will provide hands-on environmental advice and support across multiple operational sites. The role includes regular site travel within greater Melbourne and visits to regional Victoria and Tasmania as required.

You will combine field inspections with office-based planning, reporting and stakeholder engagement. The role offers an indicative mix of one to two days in Port Melbourne, one day working from home and the remaining time at operational sites, depending on business needs.

About the Role
  • Partner with site managers and operations teams to understand environmental obligations, manage risks and improve performance.
  • Undertake site inspections, environmental compliance verifications and aspects and impacts register reviews, and track corrective actions through to completion.
  • Maintain environmental management plans, registers and operating conditions, and support ground disturbance processes.
  • Coordinate monitoring programs, including water and dust, and review, analyse and report data within required timeframes.
  • Support regulator liaison, regulatory reporting, incident investigations and the management of environmental complaints.
  • Coach site teams, deliver environmental education and support regional improvement plans and the organisation’s environmental strategy.
About You
You are an experienced environmental practitioner who is comfortable in both a site environment and an office. You build credibility with operational teams, negotiate practical solutions and know when an issue needs to be escalated.
  • A relevant environmental tertiary qualification, preferably Environmental Science or Environmental Engineering.
  • At least five years of relevant environmental experience in heavy industry or a regulator environment. Construction, mining, manufacturing, waste and operational facility experience are valued, as is relevant consulting experience.
  • A track record of providing practical environmental support in complex environments, with sound knowledge of regulations, management systems and processes.
  • Experience with site inspections, monitoring, environmental reporting and stakeholder engagement, including regulators.
  • Strong communication and organisation skills, a pragmatic approach and the ability to manage competing priorities across multiple sites.
  • Confidence using environmental information systems and technology, with an interest in improving how work is done.
  • Ability and willingness to travel to operational sites across Victoria and Tasmania.
Breadth of experience is particularly valuable. If you have a strong construction background and experience in other operational or consulting settings, this role offers an opportunity to bring that knowledge into an ongoing operational portfolio.
What is on offer
  • Up to $150,000 base salary plus superannuation and a $17,000 motor vehicle allowance.
  • A permanent full-time role with varied site exposure and support from an experienced Senior Environmental Business Partner.
  • A Port Melbourne base with secure parking, flexibility in work location around business needs and one day working from home.
  • The opportunity to broaden your experience across a major Australian construction materials business.
How to Apply
If you’re ready to shape the future of environmental practice and build capability within a national brand known for excellence and growth, apply today with your cover letter and resume or contact Nicki at Hinchen Recruitment Group in confidence to learn more.

Call: 0458 001 260 or email: nicki@hinchen.com.au
